That looks like a mold/mildew; both thrive in a moist environment. I would let the very wet looking soil dry out completely, and only water again once your plants start to wilt.
It is raining season now here, today was the first really sunny day in almost two weeks. I will try to move the pots to a place more protected from weather.
Did you use the same soil for all these plants?
Yes, a mixture of earth, sand, vermiculite and earthworm compost. All the pots have drainage hole, a layer of gravel, sand and a drainage cloth (no idea how it is called in English).
Can you remember if the spots are starting on the top or bottom side of the leaf?

They only appear on the top.

Here are some closeups.

Apparently leaf spot on top is more likely to be fungal or bacterial while spots on bottom is usually insect born.

Your soil could be contaminated. You could prune all the plants as much as possible. And remove them from the pots and put them in a bit of water. Burn the cuttings, use a lid. Get a foil pan and cook all the soil in the oven or fire it on a grill.

You could also just start over. Make sure you fire your soil first, though. Starting from seeds, although slower, greatly reduces the chance of introducing disease into your garden.
